manualReview.scope: Model/editor text and pedagogy pass for the owner-authorized Lessons 0014–0020 extension; not an independent human review.

englishNaturalness.evidence: The room-choice exchange is short and plausible for a community-center registration desk; 'Room one or room two?' and 'Room two, please.' are natural elliptical service-context English.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Checked every Persian title, instruction, turn translation, prompt and option explanation against the intended English meaning; wording stays simple and avoids forbidden Arabic orthographic forms.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: The Lesson introduces only room plus two numbers, reuses or/please, and finishes with hidden retrieval of a changed room choice.

distractorQuality.evidence: Room-number choices contrast the two taught numbers and a known non-room object without relying on spelling tricks.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: Iris and Nina continue their established community-center relationship with a concrete new event: choosing a room.

difficultyFit.evidence: Three small lexical targets plus one familiar choice pattern keep the load appropriate for early A1.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: The guided model uses room two while the scored retrieval switches to room one, so repetition changes the answer rather than cloning it.

transferQuality.evidence: The familiar or-choice from drinks is transferred to room numbers and location language is extended to numbered rooms.

overallCoherence.evidence: All tasks support one job: understand and state a room number.

learnerExperience.evidence: Static content-flow review only: prompts, explicit help and per-option feedback reduce dead ends, but no real learner, microphone, timing or perception test has been performed.

limitations: Real learner outcomes and delayed retention have not been measured.
Generated audio has not received a perceptual or prosody review.
Exact-match retrieval recognizes bounded patterns; valid alternative English can fall outside its answer list.
